title: GlobalFoundries to make key AI chip component for TSMC in $2 billion deal
source_used: The Register; Tom's Hardware (via Google News decode)
key_facts: GlobalFoundries announced a $2 billion partnership with TSMC on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
It will produce silicon interposers for TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging at its Malta, New York fab.
Interposers sit under compute and memory chips and give a faster, lower-power path between them than organic packaging.
Volume production will not begin until the first half of 2028 at the earliest; the deal runs five years with an option to extend.
TSMC's own Arizona packaging site and its Amkor partner site are not expected before 2028 and 2029 (The Register).
Capacity to be installed is not disclosed (Tom's Hardware).
quote_evidence: GlobalFoundries will produce silicon interposers for TSMC's chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) advanced packaging spec at its Malta, New York fab site.
GlobalFoundries, for its part, plans to add additional capacity at its Malta plant to meet demand, but volume production won't begin until the first half of 2028 at the earliest.
The companies have not disclosed the production capacity to be installed, but the agreement provides a framework for additional expansion depending on demand.
why_it_matters_hint: Gives TSMC a US source for a key packaging part, but volume starts only in 2028.
notes: Reuters original (401) unreadable; read The Register (own reporting on the company announcement) and Tom's Hardware (quotes GlobalFoundries executive Ed Kaste). Reuters headline carries the same deal.
